situation:
You are the financial analyst for TALLOWFORD MEDICAL SYSTEMS, a manufacturer that has built infusion pumps for hospitals for more than forty years. The vice president of finance (judge) has asked you to recommend which of two joint venture terms the company should accept.

TALLOWFORD MEDICAL SYSTEMS has always sold on its name. Hospitals buy its pumps because the brand has meant reliability for four decades, and purchasing committees have paid a premium for it. VIREO DEVICES, a new entrant that started shipping three years ago, now sells a simpler pump for far less, and it has taken share in every region where the two compete. The board wants the company to answer that pump with a low-cost line of its own within a year.

BRAEWOOD SURGICAL, a contract manufacturer, has offered to build that line as a joint venture and has put two terms on the table. Under the first, TALLOWFORD MEDICAL SYSTEMS pays half of the tooling cost and takes half of the profit. That half comes out of the cash reserve already committed to replacing the plant's overdue packaging equipment, and the production crew that runs it would wait another year.

Under the second term, BRAEWOOD SURGICAL pays all of the tooling and takes eighty percent of the profit. The company spends nothing now, which is why the operations group likes it, but BRAEWOOD SURGICAL would own the design and could sell the same pump under its own name, so the TALLOWFORD brand would disappear from the fastest-growing part of the market. Whichever term is signed, the split is fixed for the life of the product.

The vice president of finance (judge) wants you to weigh the two terms against what the low-cost segment is doing, identify what each one does to profit, and recommend one. The vice president of finance (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the vice president of finance (judge) of TALLOWFORD MEDICAL SYSTEMS. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have watched VIREO DEVICES take share for three years and you agree the company needs a low-cost line. What you have not settled is which of the two joint venture terms from BRAEWOOD SURGICAL to sign. You want the financial analyst to recommend one of them and then walk you through exactly how it would be carried out.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: What would you do first if we accept the term you recommend?
Who inside the company does the work after that?
